kicker: The fly connectome as a substrate

scenes.headline: What a fly's wiring diagram can and can't compute
scenes.sub: The male fruit-fly connectome, and three ways to ask what wiring is for.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Domino! The whole nervous system of a male fruit fly has been mapped, neuron by neuron. Here's what that map is, and what it can compute.

scenes.text: A connectome is a substrate, not a model: it fixes who connects to whom, and every model supplies the rest itself.
scenes.say: The idea: that map is a substrate, not a model. Weights, timing and neuromodulation are not in it; every model supplies them itself.

scenes.title: How a wiring diagram is made

items.text: Image the brain slice by slice
items.say: Electron microscopy images the brain slice by slice, at nanometer resolution.

items.text: Trace every neuron through the stack
items.say: Software traces each neuron through thousands of sections, and people proofread the result.
It finds every synapse, and a classifier guesses which transmitter each one releases.
The output is a graph: who connects to whom, and how many contacts back each link.

scenes.title: Three ways to use the wiring

steps.say: One: copy the visual wiring exactly, and train only what anatomy leaves open. Seven hundred and thirty-four parameters for over forty-five thousand neurons.
It predicted the tuning of real, named cells it never saw. A random network the same size did worse.
Two: freeze everything and train only a linear readout. Scramble the wiring, keep its statistics, and it ties.
Three: put it in a simulated body, and ask what real mass and contact forces demand of any controller.

scenes.title: Iterations to 90% accuracy
scenes.note: all end above 99%: faster learning, same ceiling
scenes.say: In an escape circuit, real wiring reached ninety percent in about thirty iterations; shuffled wiring took seventy-seven. Same final accuracy: a better starting point, not a requirement.

scenes.text: The connectome matters exactly when you care about which neuron, not just how many.
scenes.mark: which neuron, not just how many
scenes.say: So the connectome matters exactly when you care about which neuron, not just how many.

recap: A map of contacts, not a simulation
Readouts see statistics; named cells need identity
Real wiring learned faster, not better
scenes.say: To recap: a map of contacts, not a model. Readouts see its statistics; named cells need its identity.
